newsitem.title: UK: Funds positive on Japan stocks, shun bonds - Merrill.
newsitem.headline: Funds positive on Japan stocks, shun bonds - Merrill.

text.p: Japan-based fund managers plan to be big buyers of local equities but sellers of Japanese bonds, a survey by Merrill Lynch said.
The survey, which covered 42 funds managing $550 billion, found that buyers of Japanese bonds outnumber sellers by 46 percent.
In contrast sellers of Japanese bonds outnumber buyers by 44 percent, the highest number since the survey began in 1994.
"The Japanese bond market is friendless; 88 percent of respondents are bears on a year's view. The rest are neutral. There was not even a single bull," the survey said.
Fund managers are seen as wishing to build up their equity exposure, Merrill said.

"Japanese equities are benefiting from an equity-friendly environment. Analysts should continue to upgrade their forecasts for corporate earnings, especially for companies exposed to the domestic economy," said Bijal Shah, global strategist at Merrill Lynch.
Within the equity markets, fund managers prefer manufacturers to financial stocks, with banks and securities houses particularly shunned.

In contrast to fund managers in the U.S. and Europe, who turned negative on Europe after the Socialist victory in France, Japan-based fund managers remain positive, with 17 percent more buyers than sellers.
Japan-based fund managers see local interest rates rising; 81 percent expect a rise in the Discount Rate.

Japan-based managers plan to be sellers of cash, with 20 percent more sellers than buyers. But Japan funds are still large holders of cash, with an average allocation of 15 percent, the survey showed.
Gallup conducted the survey for Merrill Lynch between June 2 and 3. - James Saft, London newsroom +171 542 2734
